Clicking on col 23 was no_impact. So clicking on an empty cell that's not adjacent to a tile doesn't move the selected tile. Let me reconsider the mechanic.
Looking at all my experiments:
1. Clicked col 26 (inside p tile) → p selected, N moved right by 1 (18-21→18-21, wait no, N was at 17-20 and moved to 18-21)
2. Clicked col 35 (inside b tile) → b selected
3. Clicked col 22 (adjacent to N) → N selected
4. Clicked col 27 (inside p tile) → p selected
5. Clicked col 23 (empty, not adjacent to any tile) → no_impact
So the mechanic seems to be: clicking on a tile selects it. Clicking on an empty cell adjacent to a tile selects that tile. Clicking on an empty cell NOT adjacent to any tile does nothing.
But what about moving? When I clicked col 26 (inside p), N moved right by 1. That was the first action. Let me re-examine: N was at 17-20, after clicking col 26, N moved to 18-21. The p tile was at 26-29. So clicking inside p moved N right by 1. That's strange.
Wait, maybe the mechanic is: clicking on a tile moves the PREVIOUSLY selected tile 1 cell toward the click, and also selects the clicked tile. So:
- Initially, N was selected (from the first click at col 26... no, the first click was col 26)
Actually, let me re-trace from the beginning:
1. First action (from previous conversation): MOUSE(58,26) → N moved from 17-20 to 18-21, white frame appeared around p (25-30)
2. MOUSE(58,40) → no_impact (empty space, not adjacent to any tile)
3. MOUSE(58,35) → b selected (white frame at 33-38)
4. MOUSE(58,22) → N selected (white frame at 17-22), b not moved
5. MOUSE(58,27) → p selected (white frame at 25-30), N not moved
6. MOUSE(58,23) → no_impact
So in step 1, clicking on col 26 (inside p) moved N right by 1 and selected p. In step 4, clicking on col 22 (adjacent to N) selected N but didn't move b. In step 5, clicking on col 27 (inside p) selected p but didn't move N.
The difference between step 1 and steps 4-5: in step 1, N was the selected tile and clicking inside p moved N. In steps 4-5, the selected tile was different and clicking on a tile just changed the selection.
Wait, maybe in step 1, N wasn't selected - maybe the initial state had no selection, and clicking on col 26 selected p and moved N as a side effect. Or maybe the initial state had N selected.
Actually, I think I need to reconsider. Maybe the mechanic is: clicking on a tile selects it. Clicking on an empty cell moves the selected tile 1 cell toward the click. But the "empty cell" must be in the direction the tile can move.
Let me reconsider step 1: N was at 17-20. I clicked col 26. Col 26 is to the right of N. If N was selected, clicking col 26 (empty, to the right) should move N right by 1 to 18-21. That matches! And the white frame appeared around p because... hmm, maybe the white frame shows the destination, not the selected tile.
Wait, no. In step 3, I clicked col 35 (inside b) and the white frame appeared around b (33-38). In step 4, I clicked col 22 (adjacent to N) and the white frame appeared around N (17-22). In step 5, I clicked col 27 (inside p) and the white frame appeared around p (25-30).
So the white frame always appears around the tile I clicked on or adjacent to. It's the selection indicator. And in step 1, clicking col 26 (which is in the gap, not inside p) moved N right by 1 and then the white frame appeared around p.
Wait, col 26 - let me check. In the original layout, p was at cols 26-29. So col 26 is INSIDE the p tile. But in step 1, the white frame appeared around p (25-30). So clicking inside p selected p. But N also moved right by 1. 
Hmm, maybe the mechanic is: clicking on a tile selects it AND moves the previously selected tile 1 cell toward the click. In step 1, N was previously selected (or the initial selection), and clicking on p moved N right by 1 toward p. Then p became the new selection.
In step 4, b was selected, and I clicked col 22 (adjacent to N). This should have moved b left by 1 toward col 22. But b didn't move - instead N got selected. So maybe the mechanic is different.
Actually, wait. Let me re-examine step 4. I clicked col 22, which is adjacent to N (cols 18-21). The result was: N selected (white frame at 17-22), b not moved. If the mechanic were "clicking on a tile moves the selected tile toward it," then b should have moved left toward col 22. But b didn't move. So maybe the mechanic is: clicking on a tile selects it (and deselects the previous), and clicking on an empty cell moves the selected tile 1 step toward the click.
In step 1, I clicked col 26, which is inside the p tile. So p got selected. But N also moved right by 1. That's the confusing part. Unless... the initial state had N selected, and clicking inside p moved N right by 1 (toward p) and then selected p.
In step 4, b was selected, and I clicked col 22 (adjacent to N, not inside N). So maybe clicking adjacent to a tile selects that tile without moving the previously selected one. But clicking inside a tile moves the previously selected tile toward it and selects the clicked tile.
That's a possible explanation but it seems convoluted. Let me just test it directly. Let me select a tile and then click on an empty cell that's clearly in the direction of movement.
Actually, let me try a different approach. Let me select the p tile and click on col 31 (empty, to the right of p, in the gap between p and b). If the mechanic is "clicking on empty cell moves selected tile 1 step toward click," p should move right by 1 to 27-30.
